findings.evidence: P2 inserts the PRIVACY.md row 'Live stuck alerts (every kit, including kits with logging off) | App memory, per class ...'. The 5.6 edge STU_DEV->ALERTS is labelled 'every kit incl. logging off'. D2 says live alerts 'are never written to the database or logs' and gives no scope. But the jade-8n2.2 close reason and jade-4a7's acceptance cover only no-log mode ('client sends only stuck/stuck_resolved there in no-log mode'). ARCHITECTURE 8 lists the memory-only alert only under 'When it is off'. The plan's own Q3 says it is undecided whether kits with logging on use the same endpoint or ingested stuck events, and that 'p7-live-stuck must not guess'. So the corrected PRIVACY.md (the source for jade-771 and the consent review under jade-bi5) and the threat-model diagram would state an answer the decision did not give. That breaks INV6. If p7-live-stuck later builds the alert view for logging-on kits from the events table, the PRIVACY inventory row is false.
findings.fix: Limit P2, D2 and the 5.6 edge to what was decided. P2 row: 'Live stuck alerts for kits with logging off'. D2: 'For kits with logging off, live stuck alerts (ADR 0017) have no table ...'. Edge label: 'stuck / stuck_resolved, logging off (logging-on path: open, Q3)'. Add a short Q3 pointer in the threat model and in ADR 0017's Consequences.
findings.path: plan 4.5 P2 and D2; plan 5.6 required edges; plan 8 Q3

findings.evidence: OB5 requires that every abuse case has a named mitigation and the phase that implements it. For AB4, ARCHITECTURE 9 names the mitigation 'Facilitator sees duplicate joins and can reset a kit's devices'. The plan gives a phase (Phase 3, jade-axr) only for the reset half. The 'sees duplicate joins' half goes to 'the filed bead'. AB12's endpoint bounding and rate limiting also go to 'the filed bead'. The 5.8 command `bd create "..." -t task -p 2 --deps discovered-from:jade-okb` sets no phase or parent epic and no description or acceptance criteria, so neither mitigation has an implementing phase. RR6 says they are 'unscheduled'. AC9 only checks that the row contains `Phase [0-9]+` somewhere, which the Phase 3 and Phase 7 cells already satisfy, so the gap passes the checks. jade-sio (p9-authz-sweep) will walk AB4 and AB12 and find nothing that implements them.
findings.fix: Propose a phase for each filed bead: Phase 7 (facilitator dashboard, the home of p7-live-stuck and the class view) is the natural owner of both. File them with that epic as parent, plus a one-line description and an acceptance line. Write the phase into the AB4 and AB12 cells, and mark the phase choice for Mike's confirmation (add it to section 8). Tighten AC9 so each mitigation clause in a row carries its own phase and bead.
findings.path: plan 5.5 rows AB4 and AB12; plan 5.8; AC9

findings.evidence: OB6 requires the diagram to show every place adult PII and kit-level data is stored. p10-backups (phase-10 line 50) says 'Perform a full restore onto staging'. After that, the staging VM holds a copy of production adult PII (users, the accounts created under jade-873) and kit-level data. The 5.6 node list has no staging store, and no edge BACKUP->staging. p10-monitoring (phase-10 lines 75-77) sends 5xx and backup-failure alerts to a Discord webhook. p3-invites (phase-03 line 36) hands invite links, which are plain tokens, to facilitators 'over Discord'. So a third party sits on two data paths, and neither the actors, the trust boundaries nor the diagram name it.
findings.fix: Add a STAGING node (staging VM DB: holds a production restore after the p10-backups drill; adult PII and kit-level data; no rule yet for when that copy is deleted, so record it as an open item or a residual risk) with the edge BACKUP->STAGING 'restore drill (p10-backups)'. Add a DISCORD node outside the VM (webhook alerts must carry no PII, codes or kit activity; invite links in transit) and a trust boundary for it. Add both node ids to AC10 and say in section 7 what is still undecided.
findings.path: plan 5.6 data-flow diagram; 5.2 actors; 5.4 trust boundaries; AC10

findings.evidence: The precedence rule says the bead wins over a phase file when its acceptance criteria cite a decision. But several beads contradict their own amended acceptance in their descriptions. jade-zg3's description still says 'Clamp client timestamps that are in the future or older than 14 days'. jade-e6m's says 'participant letter (A/B/C)'. jade-7if's says 'Rate limit per account and per IP'. jade-8vo's covers only raw events. 'The bead is current' does not tell a reader of `bd show` which part of the bead wins.
findings.fix: State it explicitly in both places: 'acceptance criteria that cite a jade-8n2.<k> decision win over the phase file and over the bead's own description'. List those four descriptions as rows in the amendment map.
findings.path: plan 4.4 item 3 (closing sentence); plan 4.6 CLAUDE.md line

findings.evidence: 5.5 specifies the table as `| ID | Abuse case | Mitigation (named) | Phase, plan key, bead | Verified by |` (5 columns), but the table shown has 4 columns and moves 'Verified by' into a paragraph. Section 6 'Retention and deletion paths' has no content outline. The retention tiers of jade-8vo do not cover class_kits (kit_id, consent_confirmed_by), kit_codes.redeemed_by or the ids in audit_log.subject. INV6 requires the doc to say so, but nothing in the plan makes it.
findings.fix: Pick one column layout for the table. Add an outline for section 6: delete_kit_data, the retention tiers, backups that outlive both by up to 30 days (RR2), and the kit-keyed tables that no retention rule covers (class_kits, kit_codes, audit_log), recorded as open.
findings.path: plan 5.1 and 5.5 table spec; threat-model sections 6 and 8

findings.evidence: AC12 requires each commit to touch only the files section 4 or 5 lists. But the plan runs `bd update --claim`, `bd create` and `bd close` around the commits, and the beads pre-commit hook (.beads/hooks/pre-commit runs `bd hooks run pre-commit`) may export to .beads/ files and stage them. .beads/interactions.jsonl is present in the snapshot. The commit could then include .beads files and fail AC12, or the implementer may unstage them by hand.
findings.fix: Say whether .beads/ changes are allowed in these commits. Either exclude .beads/ from the AC12 file-list check, or require them to be left out of the commits.
findings.path: plan 7 AC12; plan 6 order of work

findings.evidence: 5.2 says staff 'also holds VM and backup-key access, named as the insider path'. 5.7 says 'who holds VM and SSH access' stays open until jade-0za. The threat model would state as fact something it also lists as open.
findings.fix: In 5.2 write 'VM and SSH access: holder not yet decided (jade-0za); backup key held by the team (PRIVACY.md, jade-fgs)'.

findings.evidence: The title 'Step-metrics views and the retention job ship after launch' claims more than the jade-8n2.1 close reason, which only says p8-views and p9-retention are 'labelled post-launch-ok' (they may ship after launch). Only the retention job is stated to ship after launch (jade-771 acceptance).
findings.fix: Retitle it, e.g. '0016. Retention ships after launch; step-metrics views are post-launch-ok', and adjust the filename slug to match.
